subject.title: WhatsApp inter_session delivery requests can be wrongly suppressed as REPLY_SKIP / ANNOUNCE_SKIP / NO_REPLY

question: Should this WhatsApp inter-session delivery-loss issue be solved with the narrow source-reply/message-tool contract from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/97311, or deferred to the broader structured handoff contract in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/33478?
rationale: The source-level bug remains, but the permanent fix changes model-facing A2A delivery semantics and must preserve the prompt-cache and reverse-send boundaries maintainers have been reviewing across related PRs.

options.title: Review the narrow return-path PR
options.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/97311 as the current fix candidate, require its prompt-cache/security redaction concerns to be resolved, and use WhatsApp or equivalent source-reply proof before merge.

options.title: Defer to structured callbacks
options.body: Keep this issue open as a symptom tracker but make https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/33478 own the typed delivery-intent or callback API contract.

options.title: Request fresh live WhatsApp proof first
options.body: Keep the issue blocked on a current-main WhatsApp transcript if maintainers want live confirmation before accepting any prompt or API change.

recommendation.title: Review the narrow return-path PR
recommendation.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/97311 as the current fix candidate, require its prompt-cache/security redaction concerns to be resolved, and use WhatsApp or equivalent source-reply proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc has strong recent merged history on sessions_send lifecycle behavior and is a good routing owner for the A2A contract decision.
